sentences.text:
3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the revision petitioner has made out any ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the Trial Court?"

My answer to the above point is in the 'Negative' for the following:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5128 HC-KAR REASONS 4.
The petitioner as informant filed the first information with Women Police Station, Bidar against accused Nos.1 to 3 alleging commission of the offences as stated above.
The same was registered in Crime No.8/2021.
After investigation, the final report came to be filed.
The Trial Court took cognizance of the offences, registered S.C.No.86/2025.
Respondent Nos.2 to 4 being accused Nos.1 to 3, appeared before the Trial Court, filed the application under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. seeking discharge.
The said application came to be allowed vide order dated 18.02.2025.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner is before this Court.
5. The contention taken by the petitioner in the first information is that, she was aged 30 years and had developed intimacy with accused No.1.
He promised to marry her and they had physical relationship repeatedly.
Even the informant had gone to Bengaluru to meet accused No.1 and they had physical relationship there.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5128 HC-KAR
Now it is the contention of the petitioner that, accused No.1 off late refused to marry her, and thereby he has committed the above mentioned offences.

placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Jothiragawan vs. State Represented by the Inspector of Police and Another1 wherein similar set of facts were considered and by placing reliance on its earlier decision in Prithvirajan vs. The State Represented by the Inspector of Police & Another2, the Apex Court reiterated the position of law that a breach of promise to marry does not automatically amount to rape, unless fraudulent intent existed at the time of taking consent.

entities.text: Jothiragawan vs. State Represented by the Inspector of Police and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relationship between two major persons who are closely related, was presumed to be consensual.
7. Petitioner is aged 30 years.

The petitioner and accused No.1 are majors, and they have voluntarily had 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 347 Criminal Appeal No.282 of 2025 @ SLP(Crl.)No.12663 of 2022 NC:
2025:KHC-K:5128 HC-KAR the physical relationship.

It is not the contention of the petitioner that,
even while having physical relationship with her, accused No.1 had an intention to cheat her.

Simply because later he refused to marry her, the same cannot be a ground to invoke Sections 376 (2) (n)
and 417 of the IPC.

8. The decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the present case where,
the petitioner herself states that she had developed intimacy with accused No.1 and they had physical relationship repeatedly.
Subsequently, accused No.1 refused to marry her.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be said that the voluntary acts of the petitioner and accused No.1 will give rise to commission of the offences as alleged.

Considering all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that, there is no illegality or perversity in the order passed by the Trial Court and it does not call for any interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5128 HC-KAR 10.

In view of the above, I answer the above point in the 'negative' and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Revision Petition is dismissed.
